title: Blind Metaverse
summary: Nara's patent specifies AI voice control for an accessible metaverse. The Blind Metaverse demo uses speech synthesis; deployment of the patented speech recognition is unverified.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Nara's accessible-metaverse work aims to let blind users navigate virtual spaces and access information through audio and tactile interfaces. A corresponding Nara patent specifies a deep-learning speech-recognition model that interprets spoken input from a Braille terminal and controls the computing device. The patent corresponds to the ITU project through its assignee, inventor, purpose, and interface architecture, but it does not name Blind Metaverse as a product. This record concerns the intended accessibility benefit of that specified AI voice-control function. The public Blind Metaverse demo also integrates Google Cloud speech synthesis, although the exact model behind its selected Korean Standard voice is unverified. The ITU contribution reports exhibition use of the accessibility platform, but neither that account nor the inspected implementation establishes that the patented speech-recognition function was deployed or that AI produced a measured improvement. The patent is evidence of the developer's design, not an independent evaluation of outcomes.
purpose: Use AI speech recognition to provide blind users with voice control of an accessible virtual environment.
system: Nara's proposed AI voice-control function for a metaverse and Braille interface
developer: Humanities Artificial Intelligence Research Center of Nara Knowledge Information Co.

ratings.reason: Blind users are intended to gain an alternative means of controlling a virtual environment through AI speech recognition. Deployment and the extent of any AI-attributable improvement in access or independence are unverified.

ai_role.statement: Nara's corresponding patent explicitly specifies deep-learning speech recognition for user control. Its implementation in the ITU demo and contribution to user outcomes remain unverified. The demo's separate Google Cloud speech-synthesis integration is identifiable, but its exact Korean Standard voice model is unverified.

evidence.citation: Nara Knowledge Information, patent KR102807935B1, published May 16, 2025, especially description paragraphs 0163-0168. The patent specifies a deep-learning speech-recognition function for a metaverse and Braille interface. It corresponds to the ITU project through its assignee, inventor, purpose, and architecture, but does not name Blind Metaverse. This is a developer-authored design disclosure, not independent outcome evidence or proof of deployment.
evidence.title: Nara patent for converting a visual interface into an accessible tactile interface

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The contributor reports an accessibility demonstration and user feedback, without establishing the deployment or benefit of the patent's speech-recognition function. ITU publication is not an independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 7: Blind Metaverse

evidence.citation: Blind_DemoApp_iOS public implementation, commit a757db268dde983d49d7ad9b135dfe67be318f73, Assets/blindScript/JoyStickTTS.cs. The inspected implementation integrates Google Cloud Text-to-Speech and selects ko-KR-Standard-A. It does not establish the precise voice-model architecture, use of the patent's speech-recognition function, or user outcomes.
evidence.title: Blind Metaverse demo speech-synthesis implementation

produced_by: The patent proposes a deep-learning speech-recognition model that converts spoken input from a Braille terminal into control of the computing device supporting the metaverse interface.
must_hold: The specified design would require a working speech-recognition component, a compatible audio input and Braille interface, and integration with the virtual environment. Neither the patent nor the ITU account establishes conditions sufficient to reproduce a beneficial user outcome.

headline: Nara proposes AI voice control for an accessible metaverse

revisions.change: Added the specific intended AI application after reviewing project documentation beyond the collection entry. Benefit depth and outcome status remain separate from the evidence confidence.

claim_basis: The makers' report and two other sources from the makers are on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
